name: EtherRoute
target_user: Network Protocol Engineers and Systems Architects
problem: Standard userspace networking stacks hide packet routing mechanics and lack programmable flow control, deterministic queue management, and isolated congestion testing harnesses.
pain: Simulating complex packet loss, route calculation anomalies, and transport-layer reliability protocols locally requires heavy virtual machine infrastructure.
solution: A zero-dependency userspace network router and transport protocol stack implemented in Java 21, featuring a custom IP packet parser, routing table lookup engine, and reliable sliding-window transport layer.
verification: Rigorous test suite injecting corrupted Ethernet frames, overlapping subnet masks, dropped packets, and out-of-order TCP segments into loopback socket channels to verify state machine robustness.
major_features: Custom Ethernet frame and IPv4/IPv6 packet parser operating directly on raw byte buffers
Longest-Prefix Match (LPM) routing table lookup engine implemented using compressed trie structures
Reliable transport layer implementing sliding-window flow control and selective acknowledgment (SACK)
Congestion control state machine incorporating slow-start, congestion avoidance, and fast recovery loops
Non-blocking I/O multiplexer utilizing Java 21 Selector and SocketChannel primitives
Virtual network interface simulation harness supporting loopback packet injection and bridging
Deterministic network delay and jitter emulator injecting configurable latency profiles
Comprehensive traffic metrics collector logging packet loss ratios, retransmissions, and throughput
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
